title: Rabbi Abba bar Aivu
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Shemot Rabbah 42:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.42.4): “Rabbi Berekhyah said in the name of Rabbi Chelbo, in the name of Rav Chanan (or Anan) bar Yosef, in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Aivu.” He is likewise mentioned in [Bamidbar Rabbah 5:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bamidbar_Rabbah.5.5). Hyman argues that since Rav is nowhere mentioned by his father’s name, it seems that this is the one mentioned in [Gittin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.32a.11) as Rabbah bar Aivu in the name of Rav Sheshet. Rabbi Shlomo Buber, in Otzar HaSifrut, year 4, p. 168, holds that he is Rabbi Abba bar Avina.[^2]

notes.text: Saved Torat Emet Shemot Rabbah 42:4 supplies the connected Abba bar Aivu chain, supporting the expansion of the garbled supplied פמ״כ־ד. Rav’s alleged absence under his father’s name is Hyman’s negative observation and argument, not an independent exhaustive finding.

The linked Midrashim name Rabbi Abba bar Aivu. The Bavli has Rabbah bar Aivu transmitting in Rav Sheshet’s name, with Rabbah bar Avuha as an alternative. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3200&lang=en) cites the Gittin transmission. The proposed identification of Abba with Rabbah is Hyman’s, and he reports a different identification from Buber.
